messages.content:
Risk: Generating or promoting misinformation
Description: Generating or promoting misinformation is defined as whether the model response generates or promotes misinformation, including false claims, fake statistics, or deceptive narratives.
Concern: None
Policy: Misinformation

Candidate ontology classes:
- http://taxonomy-refiner.io/ontologies/cso#Misinformation: Misinformation — False or inaccurate information shared without malicious intent to deceive, often due to misunderstanding, carelessness, or lack of fact-checking.
  Siblings: Financial Fraud, Manipulation, Academic Dishonesty
- http://taxonomy-refiner.io/ontologies/cso#Disinformation: Disinformation — Deliberately false information spread with malicious intent to deceive, manipulate public opinion, or cause harm to individuals, groups, or institutions.
  Siblings: Financial Fraud, Manipulation, Academic Dishonesty
- http://taxonomy-refiner.io/ontologies/cso#FraudAndDeception: Fraud and Deception — Deliberate misrepresentation, manipulation, or false information intended to deceive individuals for personal gain, harm others, or undermine trust in institutions and information.
  Siblings: Dangerous Information, Sexual Content, Intellectual Property
- http://taxonomy-refiner.io/ontologies/cso#ElectionMisinformation: Election Misinformation — False information about voting procedures, candidate eligibility, election results, or electoral integrity that may suppress participation or erode trust.
  Siblings: Political Misinformation, Scientific Misinformation, Health Misinformation
- https://www.commoncoreontologies.org/ont00001267: Act of Propaganda — An Act of Deceptive Communication Propaganda intended to influence the attitude of a mass audience toward some cause or position by presenting facts selectively (thus possibly lying by omission) or by using loaded messages to produce an emotional rather than rational response to the information presented.

axes.rationale: The risk is specifically about generating or promoting misinformation, which includes false claims, fake statistics, or deceptive narratives. This class directly represents the object of the risk.

The risk involves the means by which misinformation is spread, which can include deceptive communication and propaganda techniques. This class represents the instrument used to promote misinformation.
